Looking at this question about cell type maturation in transplanted cortical organoids, I need to consider which cell types are most dependent on the in vivo environment for proper maturation.

In cortical organoid transplantation studies, upper-layer (superficial layer) excitatory neurons are the last to mature during normal cortical development. In organoid culture, these cells often remain in a relatively immature state because they lack the proper developmental cues and circuit context. When transplanted into a host brain environment, these upper-layer excitatory neurons show the most significant maturation because they are most dependent on the surrounding neural environment for their full developmental program.

Lower-layer neurons differentiate earlier and may have already progressed further in organoid culture. Glial cells (astrocytes, microglia) and interneurons show different maturation patterns that are less dramatically affected by transplantation.

[ANSWER]D[/ANSWER]
